### `shopping_mall_shipments`

Represents shipments created by sellers to group order items for shipping
and tracking purposes. Each shipment is linked to one seller and can
contain multiple order items via a child junction table. Shipments track
lifecycle status and timestamps, supporting robust shipping management
within the e-commerce platform.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `seller_id`: The seller who created the shipment. [shopping_mall_sellers.id](#shopping_mall_sellers)
- `status`
  > Current status of the shipment (e.g., pending, shipped, delivered,
  > cancelled).
- `created_at`: Timestamp when the shipment was created.
- `updated_at`: Timestamp when the shipment was last updated.
- `deleted_at`: Timestamp when the shipment was soft deleted, if applicable.

### `shopping_mall_shipment_order_items`

Junction table linking shipments to specific order items included in each
shipment. Enables grouping multiple order items under one shipment for
tracking and delivery management.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `shopping_mall_shipment_id`
  > References the shipment that includes the order items. {@link
  > shopping_mall_shipments.id}
- `shopping_mall_order_item_id`
  > References the specific order item included in the shipment. {@link
  > shopping_mall_order_items.id}
- `created_at`: Record creation timestamp.
- `updated_at`: Record update timestamp.
- `deleted_at`: Soft deletion timestamp, if applicable.

### `shopping_mall_shipment_trackings`

Tracking details for shipments including the carrier name and tracking
number. Each record links to a shipment in shopping_mall_shipments and
stores the carrier's tracking code for shipment tracking purposes.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `shopping_mall_shipment_id`: Linked shipment's [shopping_mall_shipments.id](#shopping_mall_shipments).
- `carrier_name`: Name of the shipping carrier (e.g., USPS, FedEx, DHL).
- `tracking_number`: Tracking number provided by the shipping carrier for package tracking.
- `created_at`: Record creation timestamp.
- `updated_at`: Record last update timestamp.
- `deleted_at`: Soft deletion timestamp; null if not deleted.

### `shopping_mall_shipment_confirmations`

Customer confirmations of delivery per shipment, including confirmation
timestamp. This table records when a customer confirms receipt of a
shipment to track delivery completion and support order status updates.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `shopping_mall_shipment_id`: Referenced shipment's [shopping_mall_shipments.id](#shopping_mall_shipments).
- `confirmed_at`: Timestamp when the customer confirmed the delivery of the shipment.
- `created_at`: Record creation timestamp.
- `updated_at`: Record last update timestamp.
- `deleted_at`: Soft deletion timestamp; null if not deleted.

feedback, linked to the corresponding order item and product variant to
ensure purchase verification. Each review belongs to a customer and
references the specific order item and product variant to verify purchase
validity. Supports soft delete with deleted_at field. Rating is an
integer from 1 to 5 stars; review text is optional.

- `body`: Optional textual content of the review.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when the review was created.

- `deleted_at`: Timestamp when the review was soft deleted, if applicable.

audit and dispute resolution purposes. Each snapshot preserves the state
of a customer's review at a specific point in time, including rating,
textual content, and associations with order items and product variants.

- `product_review_id`: Referenced product review's [shopping_mall_product_reviews.id](#shopping_mall_product_reviews).

  > shopping_mall_order_items.id}.

  > shopping_mall_product_variants.id}.
- `rating`: Star rating given by the customer (1 to 5).
- `body`: Optional textual review content provided by the customer.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when this snapshot was created.
- `updated_at`: Timestamp when this snapshot was last updated.
- `deleted_at`: Timestamp marking soft deletion (nullable).

and approval status tracking.

be recorded uniformly.
Status tracks the approval workflow state.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `actor_type`
  > Type of actor who submitted the request, e.g., 'customer' or 'seller',
  > indicating polymorphic ownership.
- `reason`
  > Reason provided by the requester explaining why they want to become an
  > administrator.
- `status`
  > Current approval status of the request - one of 'pending', 'approved', or
  > 'rejected'.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when the request was created.
- `updated_at`: Timestamp when the request was last updated.
- `deleted_at`
  > Timestamp indicating when the request was softly deleted (null if not
  > deleted).

### `shopping_mall_administrator_grades`

Administrator roles and grades including super administrator designation.
This table defines the various administrator roles in the platform with
their corresponding hierarchical grade levels and a flag indicating
whether the role is a super administrator role with elevated privileges.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `name`
  > Name of the administrator role, e.g., "regular administrator", "super
  > administrator".
- `grade`
  > Grade level representing hierarchical rank; higher number indicates
  > higher privilege.
- `super_administrator`
  > Indicates whether this role is a super administrator with elevated
  > permissions.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when this record was created.
- `updated_at`: Timestamp when this record was last updated.
- `deleted_at`: Timestamp when this record was soft deleted; NULL if active.

### `shopping_mall_seller_approvals`

Seller registration approvals capturing approval status and optional
rejection reasons for seller accounts. Links to the seller account and
tracks timestamps for creation, updates, and optional soft deletion.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `shopping_mall_seller_id`
  > The seller account this approval is associated with. {@link
  > shopping_mall_sellers.id}
- `status`
  > Approval status of the seller registration. Valid values: 'pending',
  > 'approved', 'rejected'
- `rejection_reason`
  > Reason provided for rejection if status is 'rejected'. Null if no
  > rejection.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when this approval record was created.
- `updated_at`: Timestamp when this approval record was last updated.
- `deleted_at`
  > Timestamp indicating when this approval record was soft deleted; null if
  > active.

### `shopping_mall_product_categories`

Product categories for organizing products into hierarchical structure
with support for one level of subcategories. Categories have unique names
and descriptions, and support soft deletion for historical record
keeping.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `name`: Unique name of the product category.
- `description`: Detailed description of the product category.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when the category was created.
- `updated_at`: Timestamp when the category was last updated.
- `deleted_at`: Timestamp when the category was deleted; null if active.

### `shopping_mall_product_subcategories`

Product subcategories linked to their parent product categories. Each
subcategory has a name and description to categorize products within a
specific hierarchical structure. This table is essential for organizing
products into a two-level category system for browsing and filtering. The
parent category is referenced via foreign key relation to
shopping_mall_product_categories.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `shopping_mall_product_category_id`
  > Reference to the parent product category's
  > shopping_mall_product_categories.id.
- `name`: Name of the product subcategory for identification and display.
- `description`: Detailed description about the product subcategory's purpose and contents.
- `created_at`: The creation timestamp of this subcategory record.
- `updated_at`: The last updated timestamp of this subcategory record.
- `deleted_at`: Timestamp for soft deletion; null if not deleted.

### `shopping_mall_banned_users`

Records banned users who are either customers or sellers, including the
reason for the ban and timestamps for tracking ban history and audit
purposes. Ensures compliance with polymorphic ownership rule by having
separate nullable foreign keys to customers and sellers. Supports
administrative user-access restrictions.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `shopping_mall_customer_id`: The banned customer's [shopping_mall_customers.id](#shopping_mall_customers).
- `shopping_mall_seller_id`: The banned seller's [shopping_mall_sellers.id](#shopping_mall_sellers).
- `ban_reason`: The reason for banning the user, provided by administrators.
- `created_at`: Timestamp of when the ban record was created.
- `updated_at`: Timestamp of the most recent update to the ban record.
- `deleted_at`: Timestamp of when the ban was lifted (soft delete).

### `shopping_mall_administrative_audit_logs`

Administrative audit logs for tracking actions and changes performed by
administrators in the shopping mall platform. Each record captures the
type of action, the target entity affected, detailed description of the
change, and references the administrator who performed the action. This
enables robust audit trails for security, compliance, and accountability
within the administrative domain.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `administrator_id`
  > Administrator who performed the action. {@link
  > shopping_mall_administrators.id}
- `action_type`: Type of action performed (e.g., create, update, delete, suspend).
- `target_entity`: Name of the entity/table affected by the action.
- `target_id`: Primary key id of the target entity affected by the action.
- `action_description`: Detailed description of the action performed.
- `action_data`: Additional data or metadata related to the action, stored as JSON string.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when the audit log was created.
- `updated_at`: Timestamp when the audit log was last updated.
- `deleted_at`: Timestamp when the audit log was soft deleted (nullable for active logs).

### `shopping_mall_seller_suspensions`

Suspension records for sellers including suspension reasons and
timestamps. Each record references one seller in shopping_mall_sellers.
Supports soft deletion via nullable deleted_at. Used for administrative
account suspension management.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `seller_id`: Belonged seller's [shopping_mall_sellers.id](#shopping_mall_sellers).
- `suspension_reason`: Reason for suspending the seller account.
- `suspended_at`: Datetime when the seller was suspended.
- `created_at`: Record creation timestamp.
- `updated_at`: Record last update timestamp.
- `deleted_at`: Record soft deletion timestamp; null if active.

# E-Commerce Shopping Mall Platform

## Customer Account

- Customers sign up with email and password
- Customers log in with email and password
- Customers can change their password
- Customers can delete their account

## Customer Profile

- Each customer has a profile with: display name and phone number
- Customers can edit their display name and phone number

## Address Management

- Customers can add multiple shipping addresses
- Each address has: recipient name, phone number, street address, city, state/province, postal code, country
- Customers can edit their addresses
- Customers can delete their addresses
- Customers can set one address as the default shipping address

## Seller Account

- Sellers sign up with email and password
- Sellers log in with email and password
- Sellers can change their password
- Sellers can view their approval status (pending, approved, rejected)
- If rejected, sellers can view the rejection reason
- Rejected sellers can submit a new registration request
- Sellers can delete their account

## Seller Profile

- Sellers can edit their shop name, description, and logo
- Customers can view seller profiles

## Categories

- Customers can browse the list of all categories
- Customers can view products within a category

## Products

- Sellers can create products
- Sellers can edit their own products
- Sellers can delete their own products
- Sellers can view snapshots of their own products
- Administrators can view snapshots of any product

## Product Images

- Sellers can upload multiple images for each product
- Sellers can reorder images
- Sellers can delete images from their products

## Product Variants (SKU)

- Sellers can add variants to their products
- Sellers can edit variants
- Sellers can delete variants

## Inventory Management

- Sellers can add inventory (restock) with a quantity and reason
- Sellers can subtract inventory (adjustment/loss) with a quantity and reason
- Sellers can view the full inventory history of each variant

## Product Search

- Customers can search products by name
- Customers can filter search results by category, price range, and in-stock only
- Customers can sort search results by newest first, price low to high, or price high to low

## Wishlist

- Customers can add products to their wishlist
- Customers can view their wishlist
- Customers can remove products from their wishlist

## Shopping Cart

- Customers can add variants to their cart with quantity
- Customers can view their cart
- Customers can change the quantity of items in their cart
- Customers can remove items from their cart

## Checkout

- Customers can select a shipping address
- Customers can review the order summary before placing the order

## Order Creation

- Customers place orders after payment succeeds
- Customers can view order history
- Customers can view the full details of an order

## Shipping

- Sellers can create shipments with tracking information
- Customers can view tracking information
- Customers confirm delivery per shipment

## Order Cancellation

- Customers can request cancellation for individual items
- Sellers can approve or reject cancellation requests

## Refund Requests

- Customers can request a refund for individual items
- Sellers can approve or reject refund requests

## Reviews and Ratings

- Customers can write, edit, or delete their own reviews

## Seller Dashboard

- Sellers can view a summary of their shop
- Sellers can view a list of all order items for their products

## Administrator System

- Users can submit requests to become administrators
- Super administrators can approve or reject requests
- Administrators can approve or reject seller registrations
- Administrators can suspend or unsuspend seller accounts
- Administrators can create, edit, or delete categories
- Administrators can view and delete any product
- Administrators can view all orders
- Administrators can force-cancel or force-refund items or orders
- Administrators can ban or unban customers and sellers

operations.specification: This join operation creates a new customer account by accepting email and password credentials. operations.description:
This API endpoint enables new customers to register an account with the shopping mall platform.

The primary input fields are `email` and `password` which correspond to the `email` and `password_hash` fields in the `shopping_mall_customers` database table.

The system ensures email uniqueness and securely stores the password as a hash.

Successful registration returns authorization tokens encapsulated in the response type IShoppingMallCustomer.IAuthorized, which clients use to authenticate subsequent requests.

This endpoint is public and does not require prior authentication.

Flow:
- The client submits email and password.
- The service hashes the password and saves the record.
- On success, the service returns access and refresh tokens.

Errors include duplicate email and invalid input validation failures.

This operation is critical for membership onboarding and must be secure and performant.

This operation allows sellers and administrators to modify variant details such as SKU code, price override, and stock quantity. SKU codes must remain unique within the scope of the product.

The path parameters productId and variantId are UUIDs referencing the parent product and the variant respectively.

Security considerations: authorized access is restricted to the seller owning the product and platform administrators.

The entity shopping_mall_product_variants stores each variant with fields including creation/update timestamps and soft deletion status.

Request body must comply with the IShoppingMallProductVariant.IUpdate data structure, supporting partial updates of variant properties.

This operation returns the fully updated variant object in the response body.

Related operations include POST /products/{productId}/variants for creation and DELETE /products/{productId}/variants/{variantId} for deletion.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Perform validation that the specified productId and variantId exist and belong together. Verify authorization of the requesting user as either the owning seller or an administrator.

Check for uniqueness of sku_code within the given product context before applying changes.

Execute update transaction to modify shopping_mall_product_variants record with provided fields from the IShoppingMallProductVariant.IUpdate DTO.

Update the updated_at timestamp to the current time.

Return the updated variant entity as the response payload.

Handle edge cases including conflicting sku_code, invalid variant IDs, and unauthorized access with appropriate error responses.

Audit changes for traceability if applicable.

operations.description:

This operation deletes the specific variant from the shopping_mall_product_variants table, which uniquely identifies each variant by its UUID. The productId path parameter confirms that the variant belongs to the specified product, ensuring safe deletion within the product scope.

Users must ensure no pending order items or cancellation/refund requests are associated with the variant before deletion, as the operation will not perform soft deletes.

No request body is required as all necessary information is conveyed via path parameters.

This operation returns no content on success.

This operation complements other variant management endpoints such as POST /products/{productId}/variants to add new variants, and PUT /products/{productId}/variants/{variantId} to update existing ones.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
Implement deletion logic by validating existence of the variant with the given variantId belonging to the product identified by productId. Check for business rules preventing deletion if there are pending orders or refund requests for the variant.

Perform a hard delete of the variant record from the shopping_mall_product_variants table in a transactional manner to maintain data integrity.

Ensure cascading effects on related inventory and order data as appropriate.

Return 204 No Content status upon successful deletion.

Handle error conditions such as variant not found or invalid productId with appropriate 404 or 400 statuses.

Log deletion actions for audit purposes.

No request body is expected or processed.

This operation allows filtering by product name, category ID, and creation dates with pagination support.

Only authorized administrators or auditors with read-only access are permitted to use this endpoint, ensuring secure and controlled access to historical product data.

The operation supports robust validation of search criteria and returns a paginated summary list optimized for administrative and reporting interfaces.

Related API operations include `GET /shoppingMall/administrator/products/{productId}/snapshots` for individual snapshot access.

No soft delete is implemented on snapshot entities; snapshots are permanently stored as read-only records.

Validation and error handling ensure consistent input validation and meaningful error responses for clients.

This API supports audit and history features of the shopping mall platform, enabling visibility into product changes over time.

This is an internal operation used to archive product states and should have restricted access.

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of sales product listings with detailed filtering, sorting, and pagination capabilities.

This endpoint allows clients to search sales by product name, category, seller, status, and other attributes. It supports filtering by category ID, seller ID, partial name matching, and status (e.g., approved, pending, rejected). Pagination parameters such as page number and page size enable handling large data sets efficiently.

The request body schema is defined as IShoppingMallSale.IRequest, describing filtering, sorting, and pagination criteria used to perform the search.

The response body schema is IPageIShoppingMallSale.ISummary, which provides a paginated list of sale summaries matching the search criteria.

The response includes sale summaries with product name, base price, main category, seller information, and thumbnail images. This endpoint is critical for product search interfaces, category browsing, and administrative overview.

Security considerations allow viewing by authorized users, with potential filtering based on role.

This operation relies on the shopping_mall_sales table and related tables such as shopping_mall_sale_images for thumbnails and shopping_mall_product_categories for category details.

Related operations include GET /sales/{saleId} to fetch detailed sale information, POST /sales to create a new sale (admin or seller), PUT /sales/{saleId} to update a sale, and DELETE /sales/{saleId} to erase a sale.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Implement a search query on the shopping_mall_sales table with filters for name, category_id, seller_id, and status provided in the request body. Perform text search on product names using trigram indexes if available. Include pagination parameters (page number, page size) in the query with cursors or offsets.

Join with shopping_mall_sale_images to fetch the first image as the thumbnail for each sale. Join with shopping_mall_product_categories to retrieve category metadata.

Validate user authorization for seller or administrator roles to tailor visible data.

Return a paginated response with summaries containing sale id, name, base price, main category name, seller id, and thumbnail image URL.

Handle edge cases such as no results found, invalid filters, and pagination limits.

Ensure all query parameters map precisely to schema fields to maintain strict type safety and data integrity.

Follow typical patterns for PATCH search operations with complex filters in NestJS and Prisma environment.

operations.description:
Create a new sale listing in the shopping mall platform.

This operation allows authenticated sellers to create new product sale listings by inserting records into the `shopping_mall_sales` table.

Upon creation, an immutable snapshot capturing the initial sale state is generated for audit and dispute resolution purposes.

Authorization is required: only authenticated sellers with valid credentials can perform this action.

The sale's status is typically set to `pending` upon creation, awaiting administrative approval through the statuses maintained in related entities.

Input data is validated against business rules such as unique product names within a category and valid pricing formats.

Upon successful creation, the complete sale entity conforming to the `IShoppingMallSale` schema is returned.

Related operations include:
- `GET /shoppingMall/seller/sales/{saleId}` to retrieve sale details
- `PUT /shoppingMall/seller/sales/{saleId}` to update sale listings
- `DELETE /shoppingMall/seller/sales/{saleId}` to remove sales

This API is integral to the seller's product catalog management workflow.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Validate seller authentication.
Validate request body for required fields including seller_id, category_id, name, description, base_price, status.
Insert new sale record into the shopping_mall_sales table.
Set created_at and updated_at timestamps.
Set deleted_at to null.
Default status to 'pending' if not provided.
Return the complete newly created sale record.
Handle database constraints and errors such as duplicate names or invalid category references.
Trigger any necessary post-creation hooks such as cache updates or notifications.

requestBody.description: New sale listing creation data

responseBody.description: Newly created sale entity conforming to IShoppingMallSale schema

operations.description:
Update an existing sale listing identified by its unique sale ID.

This API endpoint allows authorized sellers or administrators to modify sale details including name, description, base price, category association, and status. The operation ensures that the sale is active (not logically deleted) and belongs to the authorized user.

The underlying data structure is represented by the `shopping_mall_sales` table, which contains fields such as `id` (UUID primary key), `seller_id` (UUID foreign key referencing the seller), `category_id` (UUID foreign key referencing the product category), `name` (string), `description` (string), `base_price` (double precision float), `status` (string indicating sale availability and approval states), `created_at`, `updated_at`, and `deleted_at` (optional timestamp indicating logical deletion).

Authorization checks are enforced to ensure that only the owning seller or administrative users can perform this update.

Related operations include `GET /sales/{saleId}` for retrieving sale details and `POST /sales` for creating new sale listings.

Validation rules apply to the `IShoppingMallSale.IUpdate` DTO used in the request body, ensuring required fields are properly provided and formatted.

Error handling returns appropriate status codes for invalid or unauthorized requests as well as for non-existent sale IDs.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Implement this API operation as a PUT method on /sales/{saleId} that:
- Validates the saleId path parameter as a UUID string.
- Validates the request body conforms to IShoppingMallSale.IUpdate DTO.
- Verifies the invoking user is authorized (seller owner or admin) before proceeding.
- Performs a database update on the shopping_mall_sales table for the specified saleId.
- Handles updating name, description, base_price, status, and category_id.
- Returns the fully updated sale record from the database including all fields.
- Incorporates cascade updates to related entities if necessary.
- Rejects updates if the sale is logically deleted (deleted_at not null).
- Returns appropriate error responses if the saleId is invalid or sale not found.
- Logs the update action for auditing purposes.

Use transaction management to ensure data consistency.

Refer to the shopping_mall_sales database schema for field definitions and constraints.

responseBody.description: The updated sale listing details

operations.description:
Permanently removes a sale listing from the shopping mall platform identified by the given sale ID.

This operation performs a hard delete on the `shopping_mall_sales` table, removing all associated product sale data. It requires appropriate permissions from the actor (seller or administrator) who owns or manages the sale listing.

Security is enforced to prevent unauthorized deletions, and the operation verifies the existence of the sale before attempting deletion.

Upon successful deletion, no content is returned.

Related operations include creating new sales (`POST /sales`), updating sales (`PUT /sales/{saleId}`), and viewing sales details (`GET /sales/{saleId}`).
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
1. Validate the saleId path parameter as a valid UUID.
2. Verify actor's authorization to delete the sale (must be seller owning the sale or admin).
3. Perform a hard delete on the `shopping_mall_sales` table where id = saleId.
4. Enforce cascading deletion or cleanup of related data as needed (e.g., sale_images, sale_variants).
5. Return HTTP 204 No Content on success.
6. Return HTTP 404 Not Found if saleId does not exist.
7. Return HTTP 403 Forbidden if authorization fails.

The records are derived from the immutable shopping_mall_sale_snapshots table, with each snapshot linked to its original sale entity. Filtering parameters enable selection by category, price ranges, creation dates, and search keywords within titles or descriptions.

This endpoint requires administrator level authorization due to the sensitive nature of historical snapshot data. It integrates pagination for performance and efficient browsing.

Related operations include GET /sales for current sales and GET /sales/{saleId} for specific sale details.

Error handling covers invalid filters and pagination parameters with appropriate error responses.

It requires the client to provide the notification template ID, owner ID and type, notification title and body, and optionally a URL and image URL. The notification is initially marked as unread and without delivery/read timestamps.

This operation is critical for delivering real-time or batch notifications to users including customers, sellers, and administrators. Notification content can include rich data with URLs and images.

Authorization should ensure only trusted system actors or administrators invoke this endpoint to prevent unauthorized notification insertion.

The operation relates closely to GET operations that fetch and mark notifications as read.

Validation rules:
- notification_template_id, owner_id are UUIDs
- owner_type must be one of 'customer', 'seller', 'administrator'
- title and body are required text fields
- url and image_url are optional text fields

Errors must be handled gracefully for missing required fields or invalid UUIDs.

operations.specification:
Insert a new record into shopping_mall_user_notifications with provided fields.
Set is_read to false by default.
Set delivered_at and read_at to null on creation.
Generate id as UUID on creation in the database layer.
Enforce owner_type enum constraint with allowed values: ['customer', 'seller', 'administrator'].
Validate UUID formats for notification_template_id and owner_id.
Ensure title and body are non-empty strings.
Handle database errors such as foreign key violations gracefully.

This operation requires authorization allowing only system or admin roles to create notifications.

responseBody.description: Created user notification details.

operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered, paginated list of notification delivery attempts in the shopping mall platform.

This API endpoint allows administrators and authorized monitoring systems to query delivery records by channel, status, notification template, and time ranges.

### Features
- Filter by delivery channel (email, sms, push, etc.)
- Filter by delivery status (delivered, failed, pending)
- Filter by notification template ID and user notification ID
- Pagination support with page size and cursor-based navigation
- Sort by delivery attempt timestamp

### Security
- Typically restricted to administrators or authorized systems with read permissions

### Database Relationships
- Relates to shopping_mall_user_notifications table via shopping_mall_user_notification_id
- Relates to shopping_mall_notification_templates table via shopping_mall_notification_template_id

### Business Logic
- Provides visibility into the delivery lifecycle of notifications
- Supports troubleshooting and auditing of notification delivery

### Notes
- Only non-deleted records are returned by default
- Soft-deleted records are excluded unless specifically requested
- Date-time filters use UTC timestamps

Related Operations:
- GET /userNotifications to reference notification details
- GET /notificationTemplates to browse templates

Use cursor-based pagination by attemptedAt timestamp and id as tie-breaker. Join with user notifications and notification templates tables for related data if needed. Return paged summary results encapsulated as IPageIShoppingMallNotificationDelivery.ISummary. Handle sorting by attemptedAt descending by default.

This operation creates a new notification delivery record reflecting an attempt to deliver a user notification via a specific channel like email, SMS, or push notification. It captures detailed information including which user notification it belongs to and which notification template was used for the message. The delivery status indicates whether the attempt succeeded, failed, or is pending. Timestamps are recorded for when the delivery was attempted and when it completed successfully, supporting audit trails and retry logic.

Authorization to create notification deliveries is typically restricted to system components or services that manage notifications to ensure data integrity and accuracy.

The underlying database entity is `shopping_mall_notification_deliveries`, which has UUID keys and timestamps including soft deletion support. Records are soft deleted by marking the `deleted_at` timestamp rather than physical removal, preserving historical data.

This operation is fundamental for reliable notification management and monitoring in the e-commerce platform.

Related operations include reading delivery status (GET) and updating delivery records (PUT/PATCH) for retry or correction.

No soft delete semantics apply; removal is permanent.

This operation queries the `shopping_mall_sale_view_stats` database table, which stores analytics data per sale entity with relations to the core `shopping_mall_sales` entries.

The operation returns a paginated list of view statistics records to manage potentially large datasets. Pagination parameters are expected to be handled client-side.

This operation is read-only and does not modify any data.

Security considerations limit access to administrative or analytic roles authorized to view sales analytics.

Related API operations include listing sales and viewing detailed sale analytics by sale ID.

No data modification occurs in this operation; it is for analytics viewing only.

responseBody.description: A paginated list of sales view statistics summary records

operations.description:
Create a cancellation request for a specific order item by the customer.

This operation records the customer's reason for cancellation and marks the seller approval status as pending. It uses the shopping_mall_cancellation_requests entity which tracks cancellation requests with associated timestamps for creation and processing.

Only authenticated customers may perform this operation. The path parameter orderItemId uniquely identifies the order item targeted for cancellation.

The request body must include the cancellation reason string. Upon successful creation, the complete cancellation request record is returned, including generated timestamps and seller response fields.

This endpoint is essential for enabling customer-driven order item cancellation with seller review and approval workflows.

Related operations include viewing cancellation request status, updating seller approval, and managing order item states based on cancellation outcomes.
operations.name: createCancellationRequest
operations.specification:
Implement a POST handler that validates the customer identity and authorization to create a cancellation request for the specified order item identified by orderItemId (UUID).
The request body contains a reason string describing why the customer wants to cancel.
Persist a new shopping_mall_cancellation_requests record with seller_approval_status set to 'pending', requested_at set to current timestamp, and other timestamps appropriately.
Ensure cascade deletion or appropriate data linkage backups.
Return the created record as response.
Handle validation errors for required fields (reason).
Ensure the operation cannot proceed if the order item does not belong to the requesting customer.
Emit domain events for cancellation request creation.
Include audit logging.

This operation depends on customer authentication context.

This endpoint allows authorized administrators to approve or reject a customer's cancellation request on a specific order item within the `shopping_mall_cancellation_requests` table.

It updates the `seller_approval_status` and optionally records a `seller_approval_reason` as part of the approval or rejection process. The record includes timestamps for request and processing times.

Only administrators with proper permissions may perform this operation, ensuring secure and auditable approval workflows.

The operation returns the updated cancellation request entity reflecting the approval status changes.

Clients should handle validation errors when providing invalid approval status values and unauthorized access attempts.

Related operations include listing cancellation requests and fetching individual request details.

Update the 'shopping_mall_cancellation_requests' record with the new 'seller_approval_status' and 'seller_approval_reason' values, record the 'processed_at' timestamp as the current time.

Ensure atomic transaction and error handling for invalid states or access permissions.

Return the updated cancellation request entity as the response body, reflecting all relevant fields for client display.

operations.description:
Submit a refund request for a delivered order item.

This operation allows a customer to create a refund request specifying the reason for refund related to a particular order item identified by `orderItemId`. The refund workflow involves seller approval or rejection of the request, with status tracking.

The refund request records link to the specific order item, customer, and seller. They include timestamps for request creation and seller response, refund status (pending, approved, rejected), and seller response reason. This ensures transparency and traceability of refund processing.

Security:
- Only authenticated customers who own the specified order item can create refund requests.
- Input validation is performed on the refund reason.

Database Relationship:
- Uses `shopping_mall_order_items` to identify the targeted order item.
- Creates new records in `shopping_mall_refund_requests` linked to order item, customer, and seller.

Related APIs:
- GET /orders/{orderId} to view order details and refund status.
- POST /orders/items/{orderItemId}/cancel-request for cancellation requests related to order items.

Expected Behavior:
- On successful submission, the refund request is stored and marked as pending.
- The seller is notified to respond to the refund request.
- Errors are returned if the order item does not exist or if the customer is not authorized.

This operation does not delete or modify existing refund requests, only creates new ones.
operations.name: createRefundRequest
operations.specification:
Implement service logic to create a refund request associated with the specified order item ID.
- Validate that the order item exists and is in a deliverable/refundable state.
- Verify the authenticated customer's ownership of the order item.
- Validate request body fields including refund reason.
- Create a new shopping_mall_refund_requests record linking to the order item, customer, and seller.
- Set initial status to 'pending' with timestamp.
- Send notification to the seller about the new refund request.
- Handle concurrency and possible errors such as multiple requests.
- Return the created refund request entity in the response body.

This operation requires authorization for customer actors only.

operations.description:

This operation enables a customer to confirm the delivery of a shipment by creating a record in the shopping_mall_shipment_confirmations table. Each confirmation stores the shipment ID and the timestamp when the delivery was confirmed.

Relationships:

Validation and Logic:

- Records current timestamp as confirmation time.
- Prevents duplicate confirmations by the same customer for the shipment.

Related API:
- GET /shipments/{shipmentId} to retrieve shipment details and statuses.

Expected Behavior:
- On success, returns the created confirmation record with confirmation timestamp.
- On failure, returns appropriate error (e.g., 404 if shipment not found, 403 if unauthorized).

Note: Though deleted_at exists for soft deletion, this operation always records new confirmations and does not implement deletion or soft delete behavior.
operations.name: confirmDelivery
operations.specification: The implementation must insert a new record into shopping_mall_shipment_confirmations with the shipment ID and the current timestamp as confirmed_at. Validate that the shipment ID exists and the customer is authorized to confirm it. Handle duplicate confirmation gracefully by allowing single confirmation per shipment per customer. No request body content is required; the endpoint action triggers the creation including the current timestamp. Return the full created confirmation record with all fields in the response.

parameters.name: shipmentId

responseBody.description: The shipment confirmation record that was created.

prerequisites.description: Shipment must be created before a customer can confirm its delivery.

operations.description:
This API operation allows authorized sellers and administrators to submit inventory adjustments for a specific product variant identified by variantId. Inventory adjustments represent changes to stock quantity which can be positive (restock) or negative (removal due to order or loss).

The inventory adjustment is recorded as a new entry in shopping_mall_inventory_histories linked by shopping_mall_product_variant_id to track historical stock changes precisely.

Path parameter variantId specifies the target product variant. The request body requires quantityDelta (integer) specifying units to add (positive) or remove (negative) and a reason string giving a textual explanation.

This endpoint enforces authorization checking to ensure only the owner seller or administrators can perform inventory adjustments.

Clients can expect a detailed confirmation response including the adjustment record details and timestamps.

Proper usage of this endpoint keeps inventory stock data accurate and auditable with full history preserved for compliance and operational insight.

Related API operations include GET /variants/{variantId}/inventory for retrieving current inventory status and PATCH /products/{productId}/variants/{variantId} for variant updates without inventory changes.

Soft deletion is supported on inventory history records but does NOT affect inventory calculations. The adjustment records remain immutable once created.

> MUST be written in English.
operations.name: adjustInventory
operations.specification:
1. Authorization: Confirm seller or admin roles.
2. Validate variantId is a valid UUID corresponding to an existing product variant.
3. Parse request body for quantityDelta and reason.
4. Create a new shopping_mall_inventory_histories record with:
   - shopping_mall_product_variant_id = variantId
   - quantity_delta = quantityDelta
   - reason = reason
5. Persist the inventory history entry using a transaction.
6. Calculate updated stock quantity by summing quantity_delta for all active history records.
7. Return the created inventory history record as confirmation including timestamps.
8. Handle errors for invalid variantId, unauthorized access, and data validation.

Note: This operation does NOT perform stock quantity updates outside the inventory histories. All stock calculations derive from history aggregations.

This design ensures accurate stock tracking with full historical audit trail.

operations.description:
This operation allows authorized users to resend notifications that have previously failed delivery attempts.

The notifications system maintains delivery records with statuses including 'failed'. When this endpoint is called, it triggers retries for those failed notification deliveries.

Security considerations require that only authenticated and authorized actors (such as administrators) can invoke this resend operation to prevent abuse or redundant retries.

This endpoint interacts primarily with the shopping_mall_notification_deliveries table, focusing on entries with status 'failed'. Upon execution, it attempts to redeliver these notifications via their original delivery channels.

The request body specifies criteria for selecting which failed notifications to resend (e.g., all failed notifications, by specific template ID, or by user notification ID). The response body provides a summary of how many resend attempts were initiated and any pertinent status information.

This operation complements notification management APIs that create and log notifications. It is essential for ensuring reliable notification delivery by handling transient failures.

Clients should expect that repeated calls may retry the same notifications multiple times; thus, they should consider rate limiting and idempotency at the application level.
operations.name: resendFailed

Implement a service method that queries shopping_mall_notification_deliveries for entries with status 'failed' matching the criteria in the request body. For each entry, trigger the resend logic using the associated notificationTemplate's channel information. Update the delivery record's status and timestamps accordingly. Log each resend attempt in shopping_mall_notification_logs.

Ensure the operation is transactional and handles errors gracefully, continuing retry attempts for other entries if some fail.

Authorization checks must confirm the caller's privileges to execute this sensitive operation.

Response Body Type: IShoppingMallNotificationResendFailed.IResponse

Use precise DTO schemas that define filter criteria and result summaries.

operations.description:
Update the user's notification preferences by allowing bulk modifications to enable or disable notification types across various channels (e.g., email, SMS, push). Each preference specifies the channelName, notificationType, and isEnabled flag. The operation ensures that preferences are uniquely linked to the authenticated user, represented polymorphically as customer, seller, or administrator. This idempotent operation upserts preferences, creates new entries if absent, updates existing ones, and may remove or disable preferences not included in the input. Security demands user authentication and authorization to prevent unauthorized preference changes.

The data model shopping_mall_user_notification_preferences uses composite unique keys on combinations of owner (customer_id, seller_id, administrator_id), channel_name, and notification_type, which this API enforces to avoid conflicts.

This API does not require parameters since identification comes from auth context.

The request body type IShoppingMallUserNotificationPreference.IUpdateMany supports bulk update semantics, allowing multiple preferences in one call.

The response provides the updated preferences to confirm the applied changes.

Error handling covers validation failures, authorization issues, and database conflicts.

Related operations include GET /notifications/preferences for reading current preferences and administrative notification template management APIs.
operations.name: updatePreferences
operations.specification:
The service should validate authentication and authorize the user identity as a customer, seller, or administrator.
Each preference in the request list must have valid channel_name, notification_type, and a boolean is_enabled.
The system assigns ownership fields based on authenticated user type.
Upsert preferences using composite unique constraints to avoid duplicates.
Use transactions to guarantee atomic updates.
Return the full list of updated preferences as response.
Handle conflicts (e.g., concurrent updates) gracefully with retry or error.

All fields must be validated for correctness, and sensitive operations logged for audit.

Provide meaningful HTTP status codes for success and failure states.

requestBody.description: List of notification preferences to update with channel name, notification type, and enabled flag

responseBody.description: Updated list of user notification preferences

operations.description:
Approve an administrator request specified by the unique requestId.

This operation allows super administrators to approve a pending administrator request submitted by either a customer or seller. Upon approval, the status field of the shopping_mall_administrator_requests record is updated to 'approved', indicating the request has been granted.

The requestId path parameter uniquely identifies the administrator request.

Note that the approval action triggers business logic updating the request status and other related audit trails handled in the service layer.

This endpoint is essential for managing administrator onboarding and access control in the e-commerce platform.

Security considerations: Only users with super administrator role should access this endpoint.

Related operations include:
- POST /administrator/requests/{requestId}/reject to reject requests
- GET /administrator/requests to list all requests

Expected behavior:
- Successful approval returns the full updated administrator request entity.
- If the request does not exist or is already handled, errors are returned accordingly.
operations.name: approve
operations.specification:
Perform authorization check for super administrator role.
Fetch shopping_mall_administrator_requests record by requestId.
Verify the current status is 'pending' before update.
Update the status field to 'approved'.
Save the updated record and return it in response.
Handle errors for not found or invalid status.
Ensure proper logging and audit of the operation.

The operation interacts with the shopping_mall_administrator_requests database table, modifying the 'status' column for the specified record.

If the specified requestId does not exist or is already resolved (approved or rejected), an appropriate error response should be returned.

This operation is part of the administrative approval workflow for managing elevated permissions within the shopping mall platform.

Return the updated administrator request record reflecting the new status.

Implement necessary database transaction and error handling to maintain data integrity.

operations.description:
Ban a customer by creating a new entry in the banned users table referencing the customer's unique ID.

This operation enables administrators to ban customers for policy violations or other reasons by recording the ban with a reason.

The operation requires the customerId as a path parameter, which corresponds to the shopping_mall_customer_id foreign key.

The request body includes the ban_reason property describing why the customer is banned.

Upon success, the operation returns the newly created banned user record, including timestamps and IDs.

This ensures that banned customers are tracked clearly and consistently in the system.

Authorization is expected to be restricted to administrators or authorized actors capable of managing bans.

This endpoint strictly enforces that only customers (not sellers) can be banned through this path.
operations.name: banCustomer
operations.specification:
Implement service logic to insert a new record into the shopping_mall_banned_users table.

- Validate that the customerId exists in shopping_mall_customers.
- Require ban_reason in the request body.
- Populate the shopping_mall_customer_id with the provided customerId.
- Set created_at and updated_at timestamps to current time.
- Ensure shopping_mall_seller_id is null since this is a customer ban.
- Do not set deleted_at during creation.
- Return the created banned user record as response.
- Handle errors for missing customer, duplicate bans, or database failures.

This API operation allows an administrator to unban a previously banned customer by removing or lifting the ban record associated with the specified customer ID. It targets the shopping_mall_banned_users table where bans are stored, specifically the record linked to the customer via shopping_mall_customer_id.

Security is critical: only administrators with proper authorization can perform unbanning. This ensures platform integrity and prevents unauthorized lifting of bans.

The operation identifies the target ban record uniquely by the provided customerId path parameter (UUID). Upon success, the ban record is deleted or marked as lifted, allowing the customer to regain platform access.

Clients receive the details of the affected ban record in the response for confirmation and auditing purposes.

Related operations include banning a customer, which creates ban records, and listing all banned users for review.

No request body is necessary for this operation as the path parameter suffices for identification and unban action.

The response returns the details of the unbanned user's ban record, including the ban reason and timestamps for audit trails.

This operation does not allow banning customers; it focuses exclusively on seller bans. The API consumer receives the full ban record after creation, including system-managed timestamps.

Related operations include unbanning sellers (not covered by this API) and retrieving ban records.

Return the created ban record in the response body.

operations.description:
This operation permanently removes a ban record associated with the specified seller, effectively unbanning the seller and restoring their ability to interact with the platform.

BAN RECORD DETAILS:
The banned user record tracked in the shopping_mall_banned_users table holds information about the seller ban including the reason for ban and timestamps (created, updated, deleted). This operation removes that ban record.

SECURITY & AUTHORIZATION:
Access to this operation should be restricted to authorized administrator roles with permissions to manage user bans to prevent unauthorized unbanning.

PARAMETERS:
- sellerId: The unique UUID identifier of the seller whose ban is to be removed.

RESPONSE:
Returns the details of the ban record that was removed including seller id, ban reason, and timestamps for client audit and logging purposes.

RELATED OPERATIONS:
- `POST /banned-users/sellers/{sellerId}/ban` to set a ban on a seller.
- `GET /banned-users/sellers` to list all banned sellers.

ERROR HANDLING:
- If no ban record exists for the specified seller, an appropriate error response indicating non-existence should be returned.
- If the caller is unauthorized, a 403 Forbidden response should be returned.
operations.name: unban
operations.specification:
This operation should perform the following steps:
1. Validate the sellerId path parameter as a UUID.
2. Verify that a ban record exists for the specified sellerId in the shopping_mall_banned_users table.
3. If found, delete the ban record from the table.
4. Return the details of the deleted ban record in the response for auditing.
5. Handle errors such as 'ban record not found' or unauthorized access appropriately.

The operation requires an administrator authorization actor to execute.

Database interactions:
- Query `shopping_mall_banned_users` for a record with `shopping_mall_seller_id` = `sellerId`.
- If exists, delete the record.
- Return the deleted record.

Additional notes:
- No request body is needed as the path parameter is sufficient.
- Implement transactional integrity to ensure atomic delete operation.
- Log the unbanning action in audit logs for compliance.

parameters.description: The unique UUID identifier of the seller to unban.
parameters.name: sellerId

responseBody.description: Details of the ban record that was removed to confirm successful unbanning.

prerequisites.description: A ban record must exist to be removed; thus, the seller must be banned before they can be unbanned.

operations.description:
Suspend a seller account by creating a suspension record with reason and timestamp.

This operation is restricted to administrators who have permission to control seller statuses. It records the suspension reason, the datetime of suspension, and links the record to the targeted seller account.

The shopping_mall_seller_suspensions table stores these suspensions with fields for suspension reason, timestamps for creation, update, and soft deletion tracking.

Proper validation must be performed to confirm seller existence. The operation permanently logs the suspension event.

Related operations include GET /admin/sellers/{sellerId} for retrieving seller info and POST /admin/sellers/{sellerId}/unsuspend for lifting suspensions.

Error handling includes 404 if sellerId is invalid and 400 if suspension reason is missing.

Uses the shopping_mall_seller_suspensions schema for request and response body structure.
operations.name: suspendSeller
operations.specification:
Validate the sellerId path parameter as a UUID corresponding to an existing seller.
Check administrator authorization for suspension action.
Accept request body containing suspension_reason (string) and suspended_at (datetime).
Create a new record in shopping_mall_seller_suspensions with seller_id, suspension_reason, suspended_at, and timestamps created_at and updated_at set to current time.
Return the newly created suspension record in the response.
Handle validation errors (400) and not found errors (404) appropriately.

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the seller to suspend
parameters.name: sellerId

requestBody.description: Suspension information including reason and suspension timestamp

responseBody.description: Details of the created seller suspension record

operations.description:
Unsuspend a suspended seller by administrative action. This operation removes or marks as inactive the suspension records for the given sellerId, effectively reinstating their selling privileges on the platform.

This operation affects records in the shopping_mall_seller_suspensions table linked by seller_id. The suspended_at timestamp and suspension_reason are cleared or appropriately archived to indicate the seller is no longer suspended.

Only users with administrator privileges are authorized to perform this operation to ensure platform security and compliance. Authentication and authorization checks are mandatory.

The operation returns the updated seller record from shopping_mall_sellers reflecting the current active status and suspension clearance.

Related operations include suspension management endpoints for viewing and creating suspension records, and seller account management endpoints for approval workflow handling.

Validation ensures the sellerId path parameter corresponds to an existing suspended seller; otherwise, an error is returned.

This endpoint supports the administrative workflows to maintain platform seller integrity and user trust.

**WARNING**: This operation does not soft delete any records; it explicitly lifts suspensions by clearing suspension flags or records.
operations.name: unsuspend
operations.specification:
Implement a service method to locate active suspension records by seller_id matching the given sellerId. Remove or neutralize these suspension entries, e.g., delete records or set deleted_at timestamp to mark as inactive.

Update relevant fields in the shopping_mall_sellers record if needed to reflect unsuspended status (e.g., approval_status remains unchanged but suspension effect is lifted).

Ensure transactional integrity: the suspension removal and any seller record updates must occur within a single transaction to maintain consistency.

Validate the sellerId exists and has active suspensions before proceeding; if no active suspension, return a suitable 404 or 400 error.

Audit logs might capture this administrative action for traceability.

Return the complete updated seller record as response body for client confirmation.

Strictly restrict access to admin users with appropriate permissions.

The API does not accept a request body. The sole parameter is the path parameter sellerId of UUID format indicating the target suspended seller to unsuspend.

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the seller to unsuspend (UUID format).
parameters.name: sellerId

responseBody.description: Updated seller record reflecting unsuspended status

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of administrative audit log records capturing actions performed by administrators in the shopping mall platform.

Each record details the action type (e.g., create, update, delete), the target entity and its ID affected by the action, detailed description and optional metadata of the action, as well as timestamps for creation and last update.

This endpoint supports monitoring and auditing of administrative activities for security and compliance and is generally restricted to users with administrator privileges.

The data corresponds to the shopping_mall_administrative_audit_logs database table which enforces foreign key relationship to shopping_mall_administrators for accountable actor information.

No path parameters are required.

The response provides a paginated list of audit log summaries.

Clients should support pagination via query parameters if implemented in the system, although no specific pagination parameters are defined here as path parameters.
operations.name: get
operations.specification:
Query the shopping_mall_administrative_audit_logs table to retrieve a paginated list of audit log entries.
Include the primary key, action type, target entity, target ID, action description, optional action data, and timestamps.
Join with shopping_mall_administrators table to fetch administrator details.
Implement pagination and sorting by created_at timestamp descending.
Ensure only administrators can access this data.
Handle edge cases such as no data, query failures, and authorization errors gracefully.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of administrative audit log summaries

current.description:
Current page number being viewed (1-indexed).

Indicates which page of results is currently being returned. Page
numbering starts from 1, so the first page is page 1 (not 0). This value
reflects the page parameter from the request after validation and bounds
checking.

limit.description:
Maximum number of records per page.

Defines the upper bound on how many records can be returned in a single
page. This corresponds to the limit parameter from the request. The
actual number of records in the data array may be less than this value on
the final page or when total records are fewer than the limit.
limit.x-autobe-specification: Maximum records per page. Actual count may be less on last page.

records.description:
Total count of all records matching the query criteria.

Represents the complete number of records available across all pages, not
just the current page. This value is computed via a COUNT query and is
essential for calculating total pages and displaying pagination UI
elements like "Showing 1-10 of 150 results".
records.x-autobe-specification: Total record count across all pages.

pages.description:
Total number of pages available.

Calculated as ceiling of {@link records} divided by {@link limit}. When
records is 0, pages will also be 0. This value enables clients to render
page navigation controls and validate page bounds.
pages.x-autobe-specification: Total pages. Calculated as Math.ceil(records / limit).

IPage.IPagination.description:
Pagination metadata containing current page position and total data
statistics.

This interface provides comprehensive pagination information returned
alongside paginated list data. It enables clients to implement navigation
controls, display progress indicators, and determine data boundaries for UI
rendering.
IPage.IPagination.x-autobe-specification: Pagination metadata for paginated list responses. Included in all list endpoint responses.

access.description:
Short-lived JWT access token for authenticating API requests.

This token must be included in the Authorization header using the Bearer
scheme (e.g., `Authorization: Bearer {access}`) for all endpoints requiring
authentication. The token contains encoded claims including user identity,
roles, and permissions. Typically expires within 15-60 minutes for
security; use the refresh token to obtain a new access token when expired.
access.x-autobe-specification: JWT access token. Use in Authorization header as "Bearer {access}".

refresh.description:
Long-lived refresh token for obtaining new access tokens.

Used to request new access tokens when the current access token expires,
allowing session continuation without re-authentication. Should be stored
securely and transmitted only to the token refresh endpoint. Typical
lifetime ranges from 7 to 30 days depending on security requirements.
refresh.x-autobe-specification: Refresh token for obtaining new access tokens without re-authentication.

expired_at.description:
ISO 8601 timestamp when the access token expires.

After this timestamp, the access token will be rejected by authenticated
endpoints. Clients should proactively refresh before expiration to maintain
seamless user experience. A common strategy is to refresh when remaining
time falls below 5 minutes. This timestamp is also embedded within the JWT
itself as the "exp" claim.
expired_at.x-autobe-specification: Access token expiration timestamp in ISO 8601 format.

refreshable_until.description:
ISO 8601 timestamp indicating the absolute session expiration deadline.

Represents the latest possible time the refresh token can be used. Once
this timestamp is reached, the user must fully re-authenticate with
credentials. This defines the maximum session duration regardless of
activity. If refresh token rotation is enabled, this deadline may extend
with each successful refresh.
refreshable_until.x-autobe-specification: Refresh token expiration timestamp. Re-authentication required after this time.

IAuthorizationToken.description:
JWT-based authorization token pair with expiration metadata.

Provides a complete authentication token structure containing both access and
refresh tokens along with their respective expiration timestamps. This
dual-token pattern enables secure, stateless authentication with automatic
session renewal capabilities.

The access token is short-lived for security, while the refresh token allows
obtaining new access tokens without requiring the user to re-enter
credentials. This structure is automatically included in authentication
responses across all generated backend applications.
IAuthorizationToken.x-autobe-specification: Dual-token authentication structure with access/refresh tokens and expiration info.

IShoppingMallSellerApproval.IUpdate.x-autobe-specification: This DTO maps directly to the mutable fields 'status' and 'rejection_reason' of the shopping_mall_seller_approvals table. The 'status' field accepts only the allowed values 'pending', 'approved', or 'rejected'. The 'rejection_reason' is an optional string allowed only when status is 'rejected'. Updating these fields controls the seller registration approval workflow. No other fields are modifiable through this DTO.

IShoppingMallSellerSuspension.IUpdate.description: Request payload for updating a seller suspension record's mutable fields including 'suspensionReason' and 'suspendedAt'. Used by administrators to modify seller suspension reasons and suspension timestamps.
IShoppingMallSellerSuspension.IUpdate.x-autobe-specification: This schema maps to mutable properties of the shopping_mall_seller_suspensions table. The fields 'suspension_reason' and 'suspended_at' can be updated as part of the suspension record update operation. Immutable fields such as 'id', 'seller_id', 'created_at', and 'deleted_at' are excluded. The implementation must validate existence of suspension ID, perform atomic update of the mutable fields, and auto-update the 'updated_at' timestamp.

IShoppingMallRefundRequest.IApproveRejec.description: Request payload for approving or rejecting a refund request. Includes mandatory status and optional seller response reason to be supplied by the seller or administrator.
IShoppingMallRefundRequest.IApproveRejec.x-autobe-specification: This DTO maps directly to the shopping_mall_refund_requests table for updating refund request status and optional seller response reason. The status must be either 'approved' or 'rejected'. The sellerResponseReason is optional and nullable, used to provide explanation upon approval or rejection.

IShoppingMallBannedUser.IBanCreate.description: Request body schema used to create a new banned user record representing a seller ban, containing the reason for banning the seller.
IShoppingMallBannedUser.IBanCreate.x-autobe-specification: This DTO maps directly to the shopping_mall_banned_users table for creating a ban record. The 'ban_reason' property corresponds to the database column 'ban_reason'. System-managed fields such as id, timestamps, and foreign keys are excluded from this DTO and handled automatically in the backend logic.

IShoppingMallBannedUser.IBanCustomerRequ.description: Request schema for banning a customer, including the mandatory ban reason provided by an administrator. Used in the administrator API to create a ban record associated with a specific customer.
IShoppingMallBannedUser.IBanCustomerRequ.x-autobe-specification: This schema represents the request body for the API operation that creates a banned user entry specific to a customer. It includes only one field 'ban_reason', which provides the reason an administrator bans the customer. This field is required and comes from the request body, while the customer ID is passed separately as a path parameter.

IShoppingMallUserNotificationPreference..description: Request body schema for bulk updating user notification preferences. Allows batch setting of enabled/disabled flags for each channel and notification type.
IShoppingMallUserNotificationPreference..x-autobe-specification: This DTO does not map directly to a single database table but is designed for bulk updating notification preferences in the shopping_mall_user_notification_preferences table. It captures a list of individual notification preference update requests which specify channel_name, notification_type, and enabled status. Ownership of each preference is assigned dynamically based on the authenticated user (customer, seller, or administrator). The update operation enforces composite unique constraints on (owner_id, channel_name, notification_type) to avoid duplicate preferences. Implementations must handle transactional upserts and atomic retries on conflict. The DTO encapsulates batch updates for improved API efficiency.

IShoppingMallDashboardSummary.description: Comprehensive aggregated dashboard summary for the shopping mall platform, providing key business metrics such as totals of sellers, sales, orders, customers, revenue, cancellations, refunds, products, categories, reviews, shipments, and order statuses.
IShoppingMallDashboardSummary.x-autobe-specification: Aggregates counts obtained via SQL aggregation queries on shopping_mall_sellers, shopping_mall_sales, shopping_mall_orders, and shopping_mall_order_items tables to provide a comprehensive dashboard summary for administrative and seller users. Each field represents a relevant business metric counting entities like active sellers, sales listings, orders, pending and active order items, customers, revenue sums, cancellation/refund requests, products, categories, reviews, shipments, delivered and refunded orders. This data is retrieved without pagination since it is a singleton summary view. Authorization is strictly enforced for dashboard access.

IShoppingMallSellerApprovalRejectRequest.description: Request body for rejecting a seller's registration approval, containing the required rejectionReason string explaining the denial cause.
IShoppingMallSellerApprovalRejectRequest.x-autobe-specification: This DTO is an API-specific request body schema used exclusively to provide a rejection reason string when rejecting a seller's registration approval request. It is not mapped to any database table or column.

IShoppingMallAdministratorRequest.IReque.description: Request schema for filtering and paginating administrator elevation requests in the shopping mall platform administration API.
IShoppingMallAdministratorRequest.IReque.x-autobe-specification: Implementation of request filtering and pagination for administrator requests querying shopping_mall_administrator_requests table. Includes filters for actor_type, status, created_at, updated_at, with pagination by page and limit parameters.

IShoppingMallSaleFavorite.IToggle.description:
Request and response payload for toggling a sale item as favorite for a customer. Contains the sale item ID and the resulting favorite status.

This enables clients to toggle wishlist favorites via a single API call with clear status indication.
IShoppingMallSaleFavorite.IToggle.x-autobe-specification: This schema represents the request and response payload for toggling a sale item as a favorite for an authenticated customer. The customer identity is derived from authentication context and not part of the payload. The key input is the shoppingMallSaleId (UUID) representing the sale item to toggle. The response includes the same sale item ID and a boolean 'favorited' flag indicating the new favorite status (true if added, false if removed). This enables atomic toggle operation on the shopping_mall_sale_favorites table, ensuring idempotent wishlist management.

IShoppingMallCancellationRequest.IApprov.description: Request payload for sellers to approve or reject a cancellation request. Contains the approval status and optional explanatory reason.
IShoppingMallCancellationRequest.IApprov.x-autobe-specification: DTO directly maps to the database columns seller_approval_status and seller_approval_reason in the shopping_mall_cancellation_requests table. This DTO is used to capture the seller's decision on cancellation requests, including approval status and optional reason for rejection or approval. Backend logic manages updated timestamps and validation of allowed status values ('approved', 'rejected').

IShoppingMallUserNotification.ISendRespo.description: Response schema describing the created user notification including identifiers, content, status flags, timestamps, and relationships to notification template and owner user summaries. Useful for API consumers to view notification details and metadata.
IShoppingMallUserNotification.ISendRespo.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from the shopping_mall_user_notifications database table with references to related notification template and customer owner summaries. Timestamps follow ISO 8601 format with nullable fields for soft deletion and read/delivery status. Polymorphic owner type allows 'customer', 'seller', or 'administrator' role values. URL fields are nullable. This schema represents the response data after creating or fetching a user notification.

IShoppingMallAdministratorGrade.description: Administrator grade entity representing roles with hierarchical privileges and super administrator designation in the shopping mall platform.
IShoppingMallAdministratorGrade.x-autobe-specification: This schema directly maps to the shopping_mall_administrator_grades table representing administrator grade roles, including properties such as UUID primary key id, unique role name, integer grade level, boolean super administrator flag, timestamps of creation, update, and optional soft deletion. Used to manage role-based access control within the administrator system of the shopping mall platform.

IShoppingMallSellerSuspension.IRequest.description: Request DTO for filtering and retrieving paginated lists of seller suspension records for administrative oversight via the PATCH /shoppingMall/administrator/seller-suspensions endpoint.
IShoppingMallSellerSuspension.IRequest.x-autobe-specification: This DTO is used as the request body for filtering and paginating records in the shopping_mall_seller_suspensions table. Filtering supports exact seller UUID, partial match on suspension reason, suspended date range with inclusive before and after dates, and pagination controls for page number and page size limits. The API excludes soft-deleted records (deleted_at IS NOT NULL) and sorts results by suspended_at descending.

IShoppingMallSnapshotReport.IRequest.description: Request schema for administrator snapshot report retrieval in the shopping mall platform. Supports pagination, filtering by date ranges, snapshot entity types, and status. This facilitates audit, compliance, and dispute resolution workflows by aggregating report data from all snapshot types.
IShoppingMallSnapshotReport.IRequest.x-autobe-specification: This DTO defines the request body for the PATCH /shoppingMall/administrator/snapshots/report endpoint. It encapsulates filtering options for generating reports of immutable snapshot entities across multiple tables (order, cancellationRequest, refundRequest, product, productVariant, sellerProfile). Includes pagination fields (page, limit), date filters (startDate, endDate), entity type selection (entityTypes), and status filtering for applicable snapshot types. This design supports server-side filtering, pagination, and flexible reporting requirements from administrator users.

IShoppingMallUserNotification.ISendReque.description: Request payload for sending user notifications by specifying template, recipient, delivery channel, and optional dynamic parameters to customize the message content.
IShoppingMallUserNotification.ISendReque.x-autobe-specification: The IShoppingMallUserNotification.ISendRequest schema represents the request payload to send a user notification using notification templates. It includes specifying the template by code, the recipient user ID, the delivery channel (email, sms, push), and optional parameter mappings to replace template placeholders. This schema does not directly map to a single database table but directs creation of user notification records linked to templates and owners.

IShoppingMallSnapshotReport.ISummary.description: Summary view of an immutable snapshot record used for audit, history, and dispute resolution. Contains unique ID, snapshot type discriminator, creation timestamp, nullable foreign keys to associated entities, and snapshot status fields relevant to the snapshot category. Suitable for use in administrative snapshot reports and paginated API responses.
IShoppingMallSnapshotReport.ISummary.x-autobe-specification: This schema represents a combined summary record for various immutable snapshot entities in the shopping mall system. It unifies common metadata across order snapshots, cancellation request snapshots, refund request snapshots, product snapshots, product variant snapshots, and seller profile snapshots. Each property maps directly to core columns of snapshot tables or nullable foreign keys referencing related entities. The discriminator property 'snapshotType' indicates the specific snapshot type this record refers to. This unified summary facilitates paginated aggregated reporting and filtering of snapshot records in administrative views.
