IShoppingMall.IResponse.description: Summary response for the API operation that resends failed notification deliveries. It communicates the counts of notifications considered, retried, skipped, and failed to the API consumer, along with the operation timestamp.
IShoppingMall.IResponse.x-autobe-specification: This response object is an aggregate summary of the resend attempts for failed notification deliveries. It is computed by tallying records from the shopping_mall_notification_deliveries and shopping_mall_notification_logs tables. The counts represent total failed notifications considered, how many were resent, how many were skipped due to business rules or limits, and how many resend attempts failed. The operationTimestamp marks the time when the resend operation was performed, reflecting the execution time of the resend process.

IShoppingMall.IRequest.description: Request schema defining filters to select failed notification deliveries for resend attempts. Allows clients to reliably retry delivery of notifications that previously failed, specifying templates, user notifications, delivery status, and retry time windows.
IShoppingMall.IRequest.x-autobe-specification: This schema represents the request body for the Failed Notification Resend API operation. It defines filters to select which failed notification delivery records to retry sending. Each property directly maps to a column in the shopping_mall_notification_deliveries table that is used to filter records with the status 'failed'. The implementation must query these fields with precise matching or range checks and trigger resend logic accordingly. Authorization is handled at the API level.

IShoppingMallSellerSellerDashboard.description: Summary of metrics and order item lists for the seller dashboard. Provides counts of products and order items relevant to the seller, including pending cancellations and refunds, along with paginated order item summaries. Essential for seller management of shop performance and orders.
IShoppingMallSellerSellerDashboard.x-autobe-specification: This schema represents the seller dashboard overview aggregating data from shopping_mall_products and shopping_mall_order_items. The scalar counts represent computed aggregates filtered by seller and order item statuses. The orderItems property contains paginated summaries of order items filtered and joined with related product variants and orders. Data sources include shopping_mall_products for totalProductCount and shopping_mall_order_items for order-related counts and details. Supports filtering, pagination, and status-based grouping essential for seller workflow dashboards.

IShoppingMallOrderOrderSummary.description: Dashboard summary of customer orders including counts by status and total sales amount for administrative and seller insights.
IShoppingMallOrderOrderSummary.x-autobe-specification: Aggregated summary of customer orders excluding soft deleted entries from shopping_mall_orders table, counting orders grouped by status and summing total sales and quantities for dashboard display.

IShoppingMallProductReviewProductReviewS.description: Aggregated product review statistics for a specific product, including average rating, total reviews count, and counts of reviews at each star rating level from 1 to 5. Used to quickly assess product quality and customer satisfaction.
IShoppingMallProductReviewProductReviewS.x-autobe-specification: This schema represents aggregated product review statistics computed from the shopping_mall_product_reviews table, joined with shopping_mall_product_variants and shopping_mall_products tables, filtered by productId. It aggregates average star rating (floating point), total review count (integer), and counts for each star rating level (1 through 5). These are computed fields with no direct database column mapping but derived via SQL aggregation queries optimized with index usage on product variant and product relations.

IShoppingMallSaleSalesAnalytic.ISummary.description: Sales analytics summary DTO for reporting aggregated sales data including total amount, order counts, quantities sold, and optional grouping by date, seller, or category.
IShoppingMallSaleSalesAnalytic.ISummary.x-autobe-specification: This data type represents aggregated sales analytics information computed using database aggregation queries on shopping_mall_sales and related tables. It includes sum of total sales amount, total number of orders, and total quantity sold, grouped by specified dimensions such as sales date, seller ID, or category ID.

IShoppingMallSaleSalesAnalytic.IResponse.description: A paginated response object for sales analytics summaries, containing an array of grouped sales summary records detailing total sales, order counts, and quantities, together with pagination metadata.
IShoppingMallSaleSalesAnalytic.IResponse.x-autobe-specification: IShoppingMallSalesAnalytic.IResponse represents a paginated object containing sales analytics grouped summaries. It includes pagination metadata as per IPage.IPagination and an array of aggregated sales summary records showing totals by grouping dimensions. The data is computed by querying sales and orders with applied filters and aggregates, then paginated. This object type supports administrator analytics dashboard APIs requiring efficient aggregation, filtering, and pagination.

IShoppingMallSaleSalesAnalytic.IRequest.description: Request object for filtering sales data by date range, product categories, sellers, order statuses, with pagination and sorting, enabling advanced sales analytics.
IShoppingMallSaleSalesAnalytic.IRequest.x-autobe-specification: This DTO represents the filter criteria and pagination options for performing sales analytics queries on shopping mall sales data. It includes date range filters, category and seller filters, order status selection, pagination with limit and offset, and sorting orders. The implementation requires joining shopping_mall_sales with orders on relevant foreign keys, applying filters on order creation date, categories, sellers, and order statuses. Aggregate the total sales amount, total orders, and quantity sold for each grouped result. Supports pagination via limit and offset, and sorting by date or amount ascending or descending. Errors for invalid filters must be handled gracefully.

# E-Commerce Shopping Mall Platform End-to-End Test Functions

## Customer Account Tests

- Test customer registration with valid and invalid data
- Test customer login with correct and incorrect credentials
- Test password change functionality
- Test account deletion and verify profile deletion, order preservation, review preservation as "deleted user"

## Customer Profile Tests

- Test fetching customer profile
- Test updating display name and phone number

## Address Management Tests

- Test adding multiple shipping addresses
- Test updating address fields
- Test deleting addresses
- Test setting default shipping address

## Seller Account Tests

- Test seller registration with valid and invalid data
- Test seller login with correct and incorrect credentials
- Test password change functionality
- Test viewing approval status and rejection reason
- Test resubmitting registration request after rejection
- Test seller account deletion with and without pending orders/cancellation/refund

## Seller Profile Tests

- Test fetching seller profile
- Test editing shop name, description, and logo
- Test snapshot creation on each edit

## Category Tests

- Test browsing categories
- Test viewing products within a category

## Product Tests

- Test product creation with valid data
- Test product editing and snapshot creation
- Test product deletion constraints (no pending orders or requests)
- Test viewing product snapshots

## Product Images Tests

- Test uploading multiple images
- Test image reordering
- Test deleting product images

## Product Variants Tests

- Test adding variants
- Test editing variant fields
- Test deleting variants with constraints

## Inventory Management Tests

- Test adding inventory with reason
- Test subtracting inventory with reason
- Test viewing inventory history
- Test stock calculation and out-of-stock behavior

## Product Search Tests

- Test searching products by name
- Test filtering by category, price range, in-stock only
- Test sorting options

## Wishlist Tests

- Test adding and removing products
- Test pagination of wishlist
- Test automatic removal on product deletion

## Shopping Cart Tests

- Test adding variants with quantity
- Test updating quantity
- Test removing items
- Test cart total calculation
- Test warnings for low stock or unavailable variants

## Checkout Tests

- Test checkout with valid address
- Test exclusion of unavailable items
- Test order summary correctness

## Payment and Order Tests

- Test payment success and failure handling
- Test order creation and stock adjustment
- Test order item status transitions
- Test order history listing and detailed view

## Shipping and Tracking Tests

- Test shipment creation with tracking info
- Test viewing tracking info
- Test delivery confirmation and automatic status update

## Order Cancellation and Refund Tests

- Test requesting cancellation and seller approval/rejection
- Test refund requests and seller approval/rejection
- Test stock restoration upon cancellation/refund

## Reviews and Ratings Tests

- Test writing, editing, and deleting reviews
- Test one review per product per order enforcement
- Test average rating calculation

## Seller Dashboard Tests

- Test summary data retrieval
- Test filtering order items by status

## Administrator System Tests

- Test submitting admin requests
- Test approving/rejecting admin requests
- Test seller approval workflow
- Test suspending and unsuspending sellers
- Test category management (create, edit, delete)
- Test product oversight and deletion
- Test order oversight with force-cancel and force-refund
- Test banning and unbanning users


### Test Strategy

- Use E2E testing framework (e.g., Jest + supertest)
- Use test fixtures for initial data setup
- Validate all API endpoints with expected success and failure cases
- Check database state after operations
- Simulate user roles and permissions
- Include concurrency and edge case scenarios
- Ensure snapshot creation and retrieval correctness

Ensure that the endpoint is accessible without prior authentication since this is a join operation.

dependencies.purpose:
Essential authentication prerequisite:
This join operation (post /shoppingMall/auth/customer/join) must be executed before any operations requiring 'customer' actor authorization.
It establishes the necessary user account and authentication context for the 'customer' actor, enabling subsequent API calls that depend on this specific authorization level.
Without this join operation, the main scenario endpoint and its dependencies will fail due to insufficient authentication credentials.

This confirms the authentication workflow and token issuance mechanism functions properly.

scenario.draft:
Scenario 1: Successful token refresh
- Prerequisite: Create a new customer account by calling /shoppingMall/auth/customer/join
- The customer receives a valid refresh token after join

scenario.draft:
Scenario 1: Add inventory stock to an existing product variant.

- Preconditions: Seller is authenticated and has created a product and its variant.
- Perform inventory adjustment with positive quantityDelta (e.g., +50) and a valid textual reason.
- Validate response contains the created inventory history record with the correct quantityDelta and reason.
- Verify inventory stock calculation reflects increased stock including this adjustment.
- Confirm authorization rejection if accessed by unauthorized roles is covered elsewhere (out of scope).

Scenario 2: Subtract inventory stock from an existing product variant.

- Preconditions: Seller is authenticated, product and variant exist, current stock is sufficient.
- Perform inventory adjustment with negative quantityDelta (e.g., -30) and a valid reason.
- Validate response includes accurate record and timestamp.
- Verify stock quantity decrement accounting.
- Edge case: inventory cannot go negative; proper business logic or error handling expected (not tested here as it is business logic beyond adjustInventory API).

Scenario 3: Attempt inventory adjustment with zero quantityDelta.

- Preconditions: Seller auth, product and variant ready.
- Submit inventory adjustment with quantityDelta=0 (boundary condition), reason provided.
- Validate behavior according to business rules (allow or reject zero adjustments). Usually zero adjustments are invalid; test expects rejection or no-op.

All tests depend on initial seller join authentication, product creation, and variant creation.

Dependencies must be executed in order: join seller → create product → create variant → target operation.

# E-Commerce Shopping Mall Platform Implementation Instructions

## Customer Account

- Implement registration with email and password with proper validation and secure password storage.
- Implement login with authentication and JWT token issuance.
- Enable password change with old password verification.
- Allow account deletion with cascading effects:
  - Delete profile information.
  - Preserve orders and order history for records with anonymization where necessary.
  - Preserve reviews but show as "deleted user".

## Customer Profile

- Enable fetching and editing of customer display name and phone number.

## Address Management

- Implement CRUD operations for shipping addresses with default address management.

## Seller Account

- Implement seller registration with pending administrator approval state.
- Implement login and password change.
- Provide seller approval status and rejection reason.
- Allow rejected sellers to resubmit registration requests.
- Allow account deletion only when no pending orders or requests exist.
- On deletion, remove products, preserve order history and snapshots.

## Seller Profile

- Allow editing shop name, description, and logo.
- Create snapshot on each edit.
- Enable public viewing of seller profiles.

## Categories

- Support browsing categories and viewing products within categories.

## Snapshot Principle

- Implement snapshot creation and storage for all relevant entities on every update.
- Ensure snapshots are immutable and queryable for reviews and disputes.

## Products

- Implement product creation, editing, deletion with constraints.
- Create snapshots on product and variant edits.
- Ensure variants can be created, edited, and deleted with constraints.
- Disable product visibility if no variants or deleted.

## Product Images

- Support image upload, reorder, and deletion.
- Include image changes in product snapshots.

## Inventory Management

- Implement inventory history with quantity changes and reasons.
- Ensure stock calculation by summation of inventory records.
- Handle automatic inventory adjustment on orders, cancellations, and refunds.

## Product Search

- Implement search with filters and sorting.

## Wishlist

- Support adding/removing products and automatic cleanup on product deletion.

## Shopping Cart

- Support adding variants with quantity, quantity update, and removal.
- Validate stock and availability statuses.

## Checkout

- Implement order summary and validation.
- Prevent checkout of unavailable items.

## Payment and Order Creation

- Handle payment success and failure scenarios.
- On success, create orders, decrease stock, remove cart items, and save snapshots.

## Order Management

- Track order item statuses and overall order status derivation.

## Shipping and Tracking

- Allow sellers to create shipments with tracking info.
- Update order item statuses to "shipped" on shipment creation.
- Enable customers to view and confirm delivery.
- Auto update to "delivered" after 14 days if no confirmation.

## Order Cancellation and Refund

- Implement cancellation and refund request workflows with seller approval.
- Update order item statuses accordingly.
- Restore stock quantities on cancellations and refunds.

## Reviews

- Allow customers to write, edit, delete reviews.
- Enforce one review per product per order.
- Create snapshots on review edits.
- Calculate average product rating excluding deleted reviews.

## Seller Dashboard

- Provide summary data and order item filtering for sellers.

## Administrator System

- Implement admin request submissions and approvals.
- Manage seller approvals, suspensions, category CRUD, product oversight, order oversight, user management as specified.

## General

- Implement data validation, error handling, and security best practices.
- Ensure transactional integrity where needed.
- Optimize performance for search and listings.
- Provide logging and monitoring hooks.
- Write the implementation in Typescript, NestJS framework, using Prisma ORM for the database interaction.

plan.thinking: IShoppingMallBannedUser.ICreate is collectable and maps to the shopping_mall_banned_users table. It requires either shopping_mall_customer_id or shopping_mall_seller_id and ban_reason, all present in the DTO, so no external references needed.
IShoppingMallCancellationRequest.ICreate maps to shopping_mall_cancellation_requests table. Collectable DTO for creating cancellation request records.
IShoppingMallNotificationLog.ICreate directly maps to shopping_mall_notification_logs database table, thus it is collectable and needs a collector.

The DTO IShoppingMallRefundRequestSnapshot.ICreate maps to the database table shopping_mall_refund_request_snapshots which stores immutable refund request snapshot records. This DTO is used for creation and matches the database schema, so it is collectable with no external references required.
IShoppingMallReviewSnapshot.ICreate maps directly to shopping_mall_review_snapshots table and is used to create a new immutable snapshot. It is collectable.

IShoppingMallSaleImage.ICreate is a create DTO mapping directly to the shopping_mall_sale_images table, used to create new sale image records with fields including foreign key to the sale, image URL, display order, and optional alt text. It is collectable with no external references required as all FKs are included in the DTO body.
IShoppingMallSalePromotion.ICreate maps to shopping_mall_sale_promotions. Collectable without external references.

IShoppingMallSellerApproval.ICreate is a collectable Create DTO directly mapped to the shopping_mall_seller_approvals database table representing seller registration approval records. Collector is needed to handle creation against this table by administrator actors.

IShoppingMallShipmentItem.ICreate maps directly to shopping_mall_shipment_items table. This DTO is collectable as it creates a shipment item linking order items to shipments for tracking purposes. No external references from path parameters or auth context are required since all necessary fields are in the DTO body.
Collects IShoppingMallSystemSetting.ICreate to shopping_mall_system_settings. Collectable.
IShoppingMallAdministratorRequest.ICreate maps directly to shopping_mall_administrator_requests table. It is collectable and has all necessary fields included in the DTO.
IShoppingMallInventoryHistory.ICreate maps to shopping_mall_inventory_histories table and is a Create DTO for inserting inventory history records. Collectable.

IShoppingMallProductCategory.ICreate maps directly to shopping_mall_product_categories table. It is a collectable DTO used for creating product categories with fields 'name' and 'description' provided by the client. No external references are needed as all required properties are in the DTO.
Collects IShoppingMallProductSubcategory.ICreate to shopping_mall_product_subcategories. The parent category ID is referenced from path parameter 'categoryId'.

IShoppingMallRefundRequest.ICreate is a create DTO mapping directly to shopping_mall_refund_requests database table. It represents a refund request with foreign keys to order item, customer, and seller. As the DTO contains no properties itself, external references for foreign keys are necessary from path parameters and auth context (customer). Collector will be generated for this DTO.

IShoppingMallSale.ICreate is a collectable Create DTO mapping directly to the shopping_mall_sales table. The DTO includes all required foreign keys and fields such as seller_id and category_id within its body, thus no external references are needed.

IShoppingMallAdministratorGrade.ICreate is a Create DTO that directly maps to the shopping_mall_administrator_grades table, containing necessary fields like name, grade, and super_administrator. It is collectable.

IShoppingMallNotificationTemplate.ICreate is a create DTO that directly maps to the shopping_mall_notification_templates table. It contains all necessary fields for creation, thus is collectable with the database schema shopping_mall_notification_templates and no external references.

IShoppingMallProduct.ICreate is a Create DTO mapping directly to shopping_mall_products table. seller_id FK is injected from the authenticated seller context during creation. This requires external reference for seller_id from the authorized actor. The DTO is collectable.

IShoppingMallSaleQuestionAnswer.ICreate is a Create DTO used for creating a seller's answer to a customer sale question. It directly maps to the database table shopping_mall_sale_question_answers. All necessary foreign keys (shopping_mall_sale_question_id and seller_id) are present in the DTO body. This DTO is collectable.
IShoppingMallSaleQuestion.ICreate maps to shopping_mall_sale_questions, all necessary FKs are in body, no external references needed.

IShoppingMallUserNotification.ICreate maps directly to shopping_mall_user_notifications database table. It is a collectable DTO for creating records in that table. No external FK references from path or auth context are required, all keys are in the DTO body.
IShoppingMallSaleSnapshot.ICreate maps to shopping_mall_sale_snapshots table. Collectable DTO for creating immutable sale snapshots.

IShoppingMallShipment.ICreate maps directly to shopping_mall_shipments table as indicated by 'x-autobe-database-schema' annotation. This DTO is used for creating shipment records by sellers and is collectable.
Collects IShoppingMallOrderItemSnapshot.ICreate to shopping_mall_order_item_snapshots. All FKs are in body, no external references needed.

IShoppingMallProductReview.ICreate is a Create DTO directly mapped to the shopping_mall_product_reviews table which stores product review records. It requires customer, order item, and product variant references, rating (1-5), and optional review body text. It is collectable and requires a collector to insert records into this table.

IShoppingMallUserNotificationPreference.ICreate is a Create DTO directly mapping to shopping_mall_user_notification_preferences database table, used for create or update notification preferences polymorphically owned by customer, seller, or administrator. It includes all ownership keys in the DTO body, thus no external references needed.

IShoppingMallProductImage.ICreate maps directly to shopping_mall_product_images table. The Create DTO contains all necessary fields such as image_url and display_order. No external references from path or auth context are needed.

IShoppingMallProductVariant.ICreate maps to shopping_mall_product_variants table. Collectable DTO representing product variant creation under a product. The productId foreign key is from path parameter, referenced externally.

IShoppingMallSaleReview.ICreate is a collectable Create DTO mapping directly to shopping_mall_reviews table with fields for customer ID, order ID, order item ID, rating, and optional body text. It is used for creating new reviews, so a collector is needed.
Collects IShoppingMallProductReviewSnapshot.ICreate to shopping_mall_product_review_snapshots table. Collectable.

IShoppingMallSaleUnit.ICreate is a create DTO that maps directly to the shopping_mall_sale_units database table. It contains all necessary fields for insert. No additional references from path parameters or auth context are needed as per the DTO and database schema.
Collects IShoppingMallSellerProfileSnapshot.ICreate to shopping_mall_seller_profile_snapshots for immutable seller profile snapshots. No external references needed.

IShoppingMallCancellationRequestSnapshot.ICreate maps to shopping_mall_cancellation_request_snapshots table. It is collectable and requires a database insert collector. No external references required.
Collects IShoppingMallProductVariantSnapshot.ICreate to shopping_mall_product_variant_snapshots. Collectable.
IShoppingMallProductSnapshot.ICreate maps directly to shopping_mall_product_snapshots table. It is a collectable DTO for creating immutable product snapshot records.
IShoppingMallSaleSpecification.ICreate maps to shopping_mall_sale_specifications table. It is collectable. No external references needed as all necessary foreign keys are part of the DTO.

IShoppingMallSaleFavorite.ICreate maps directly to shopping_mall_sale_favorites table, representing the creation of a customer's favorite sale item link. It is a collectable DTO requiring a collector.

Collects IShoppingMallShipmentOrderItem.ICreate directly to shopping_mall_shipment_order_items. The request body contains order item IDs and the shipmentId path parameter references shopping_mall_shipments. This is a collectable DTO mapped to database table shopping_mall_shipment_order_items with references from shipmentId path parameter and included order item IDs.
Collects shipment confirmation records mapping to shopping_mall_shipment_confirmations table. No external references needed since shipment ID is included in DTO body.

IShoppingMallShipmentTracking.ICreate maps directly to shopping_mall_shipment_trackings table. It is a create DTO for shipment tracking records. No external references needed from path or auth context as shipmentId is expected to come from URL path parameter. Collectable DTO with databaseSchemaName shopping_mall_shipment_trackings.
IShoppingMallNotificationDelivery.ICreate directly maps to the shopping_mall_notification_deliveries database table. It is collectable.

IShoppingMallSellerSuspension.ICreate maps directly to the shopping_mall_seller_suspensions table. This DTO is used for creating a new seller suspension record with fields matching the database table columns. It is collectable and requires a collector.

   * @param connection
   * @param categoryId UUID of the parent product category to contain the new subcategory.

   * @x-autobe-specification Service layer performs validation of the parent category existence using `categoryId` path parameter. It verifies that the new subcategory name is unique within the parent category context by querying the shopping_mall_product_subcategories table for existing records with the same parent category ID and name. If duplicates exist, it responds with an error 409 Conflict.

   * On success, the service inserts the new subcategory record including name and description, setting created_at and updated_at timestamps to current time. It automatically assigns a UUID for the new subcategory ID.

   * No request body fields duplicate the path parameter.

   * The response returns the full subcategory record including id, categoryId, name, description, timestamps, and nullable deleted_at.

   *
   * Errors for invalid parent category ID or constraint violations are handled with appropriate HTTP status codes.

   */
  @TypedRoute.Post()
  public async createSubcategory(
    @TypedParam("categoryId")
    categoryId: string & tags.Format<"uuid">,
    @TypedBody()
    body: IShoppingMallProductSubcategory.ICreate,
  ): Promise<IShoppingMallProductSubcategory> {
    categoryId;
    body;
    return typia.random<IShoppingMallProductSubcategory>();
  }

   *
   * This operation allows clients to specify search criteria such as subcategory name, creation date range, and status to refine the results. Pagination parameters enable retrieval of manageable data chunks.

   * The path parameter `categoryId` uniquely identifies the parent product category and must be a valid UUID.
   *
   * Only active (non-deleted) subcategories are returned unless filtering explicitly includes deleted entries.
   *
   * This endpoint is critical for frontend product browsing and category management features, enabling efficient subcategory listing and administration.
   *
   * Authorization: Accessible to administrators and relevant management actors with proper permissions.
   *
   * Related operations:
   * - GET /product/categories - to fetch overall categories
   * - POST /product/categories/{categoryId}/subcategories - to create a subcategory
   * - PUT /product/subcategories/{subcategoryId} - to update subcategory details
   * - DELETE /product/subcategories/{subcategoryId} - to delete a subcategory
   *
   * Validation rules:
   * - `categoryId` path parameter must be a UUID corresponding to an existing product category

   *
   * @param connection
   * @param categoryId The UUID of the parent product category for which to retrieve subcategories
   * @param body Filtering criteria and pagination options for the list of product subcategories
   * @x-autobe-authorization-type null
   * @x-autobe-authorization-actor administrator

   * Handle 404 errors if categoryId does not exist.
   * Validate request body schema strictly before querying.
   * Log the request details for audit.

  public async index(

    categoryId: string & tags.Format<"uuid">,
    @TypedBody()
    body: IShoppingMallProductSubcategory.IRequest,
  ): Promise<IPageIShoppingMallProductSubcategory.ISummary> {
    categoryId;
    body;
    return typia.random<IPageIShoppingMallProductSubcategory.ISummary>();
  }

  /**
   * Retrieve detailed information for a specific product subcategory within a parent product category.
   *
   * This operation allows clients to fetch subcategory data including its name and description, timestamps for creation and updates, and the soft delete status. The relationship to the parent category is implied by the categoryId path parameter, ensuring the subcategory is scoped under the specified category.

   * Security considerations require that this endpoint be accessible to authenticated users and potentially public consumers who browse product categories.

   * @x-autobe-specification Fetch the shopping_mall_product_subcategories record by its primary key 'id' = subcategoryId and verify that its 'shopping_mall_product_category_id' equals the path parameter categoryId. If not found or mismatched, return 404 Not Found.

   * Operations should leverage indexes on the primary key and unique composite key for efficient lookup.

   * Standard error handling for non-existent resources should be applied.

   * This operation is read-only and safe for cache and repeated calls.

    try {
      return await getShoppingMallAdministratorProductCategoriesCategoryIdSubcategoriesSubcategoryId(
        {
          administrator,
          categoryId,
          subcategoryId,
        },
      );
    } catch (error) {
      console.log(error);
      throw error;
    }
  }

   * Update the specified product subcategory resource under a parent product category.
   *
   * This API operation allows authorized users (e.g., administrators, authorized sellers) to modify the attributes of an existing product subcategory. The subcategory is identified by the unique composite keys of categoryId and subcategoryId. The main mutable fields are `name` and `description`.
   *

   * Key database columns involved:

   * - `shopping_mall_product_category_id` (foreign key referencing the parent category)
   * - `name` (unique subcategory name within the parent category)
   * - `description` (text description of the subcategory)
   * - `created_at`, `updated_at` timestamps
   *
   * There is no soft deletion applied to subcategory entities.
   *
   * This operation supports maintaining an organized product category tree for effective user browsing and administration.

   * Related API operations:
   * - `GET /product/categories/{categoryId}/subcategories/{subcategoryId}` to retrieve subcategory details
   * - `POST /product/categories/{categoryId}/subcategories` to create a new subcategory
   * - `DELETE /product/categories/{categoryId}/subcategories/{subcategoryId}` to permanently remove a subcategory

   * Authorization:
   * - Only authorized actors such as administrators or sellers granted edit permissions may perform this operation.
   *
   * Validation:
   * - Composite uniqueness of `name` within the parent category is enforced to avoid duplicates.
   * - UUID format validation for both path parameters.
   * - Request body schema validation for correct data types and required fields.
   *
   * Error handling:
   * - Appropriate error responses are returned for not found, validation failures, and authorization errors.

   * @param connection

   * @param subcategoryId The unique UUID of the product subcategory to update.
   * @param body The subcategory update request containing mutable fields.
   * @x-autobe-authorization-type null

   * - No soft delete logic since subcategories do not support soft deletion.

  public async update(
    @AdministratorAuth()
    administrator: AdministratorPayload,
    @TypedParam("categoryId")
    categoryId: string & tags.Format<"uuid">,
    @TypedParam("subcategoryId")

          categoryId,
          subcategoryId,
          body,
        },

    } catch (error) {

      throw error;
    }
  }

  /**
   * This API operation permanently deletes a specific product subcategory which is scoped to a parent product category.
   *
   * Only administrators are authorized to perform this action to ensure proper management and prevent accidental removal by unauthorized users.
   *
   * The operation requires both the category ID and the subcategory ID as path parameters, both expected to be UUID strings. This ensures precise targeting of the subcategory to delete, avoiding ambiguity and potential data integrity issues.
   *
   * Upon successful execution, the subcategory record is removed from the database, and due to cascade delete constraint, any related records dependent on the subcategory will also be handled appropriately, preserving referential integrity.

   * This operation is essential for maintaining an up-to-date and clean category structure in the e-commerce platform.
   *
   * Related operations include GET /categories for listing categories and subcategories, and POST /admin/categories to create replacement entries.
   *
   * Authorization: Only administrators can invoke this operation.
   *
   * Validation: The provided UUIDs are validated to match UUID format strictly.
   *
   * Error Handling: If the specified category or subcategory does not exist, the operation responds with appropriate error status (e.g., 404 Not Found).

   * @param connection
   * @param categoryId UUID of the parent product category under which the subcategory exists.

   * Return 204 No Content on successful deletion.

   * Return 404 Not Found if subcategory or category do not exist.

   * Access control will enforce that only users with administrator role can perform this operation.
   * @nestia Generated by Nestia - https://github.com/samchon/nestia
   */

  public async eraseSubcategory(

    administrator: AdministratorPayload,
    @TypedParam("categoryId")
    categoryId: string & tags.Format<"uuid">,

    subcategoryId: string & tags.Format<"uuid">,

          administrator,
          categoryId,
          subcategoryId,
        },
      );
    } catch (error) {

      throw error;
    }
  }
